extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and students of scientific method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on Baconian induction: enumerating methods of action, the twenty-seven 'prerogative instances', and practical rules for collecting experiments and observations to discover forms and laws of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuance (duration) as a method of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuance in an open vessel, therefore, is useful for separations, and in one hermetically sealed for mixtures, that in a vessel partly closed, but admitting the air, for putrefaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect instances of the operation and effect of continuance diligently from every quarter. Note that confinement impedes proper motion (leading to greater violence of motion when confined); heat (fire) stops mouldiness and similar conformations. Use duration and the degree of confinement as a deliberate experimental variable to produce separations, mixtures, or putrefaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction of motion (fifth method of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction of motion (which is the fifth method of action) is of no small use. We adopt this term, when speaking of a body which, meeting with another, either arrests, repels, allows, or directs its original motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulate figure and position of vessels (e.g., upright cone promotes condensation in alembics; reversed assists sugar refining). Use curved or alternately contracted/dilated forms and strainers to permit some portions while impeding others. Direction can be effected externally (vessel shape) or internally (e.g., pebbles in water to collect mud; egg white coagulating grosser particles in syrups). Observe and experiment with shapes and internal obstructions to direct flows and separations; note genuine results (casting, modelling) and reject rash speculative attributions (e.g., Telesius' error about animal formation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony and aversion (sixth method)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects produced by harmony and aversion (which is the sixth method) are frequently buried in obscurity; for these occult and specific properties (as they are termed), the sympathies and antipathies, are for the most part but a corruption of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish general, discoverable harmonies from superstitious 'sympathies'. Examine correspondences (e.g., bodies that differ in quantity/density but correspond in conformation, or vice versa). Investigate chemical correspondences (sulphur-type vs mercury-type tribes), harmony between bodies and their menstruum/support (climate, soil, manure, grafting), specific foods of animals, and harmony of principal with subordinate bodies. Favor experiment-backed harmonies (magnet/iron, gold/quicksilver) and seek evidence from agriculture, navigation, medicine. Because many alleged sympathies are false or mythical, inquire with diligence but avoid rash credulity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coition or union (readiness/aversion to mixture)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the ready or difficult coition or union of bodies in composition, or simple juxtaposition. For some bodies readily and willingly mix, and are incorporated, others tardily and perversely; thus powders mix best with water, chalk and ashes with oils, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record not only whether bodies mix but how they collocate, distribute, and digest their parts when mingled, and which components predominate after mixture. These observations of readiness or aversion to mixture are essential for understanding compositions and for practical manipulations in art and chemistry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation and interchange of the other six (seventh method)
rubrics_metrics.description: The seventh, and last of the seven, modes of action; namely, that by the alternation and interchange of the other six.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series or chain of this alternation is powerful but difficult to trace; do not attempt many examples until deeper investigations of the six prior modes have been carried out. Consider complex effects as chains of simpler modes acting in alternation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magical instances (definition and mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical instances ... where the matter or efficient agent is scanty or small, in comparison with the grandeur of the work or effect produced; so that even when common they appear miraculous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three ways produce such effects: (1) self-multiplication (e.g., fire, specific poisons, wheel-to-wheel transfer), (2) excitation or invitation of another substance (e.g., magnet exciting needles, leaven), (3) excess of rapidity of one species of motion over another (e.g., gunpowder, cannon, mines). Investigation of the first two requires study of harmonies; the third requires measurement of motion. Seek such instances with care; they may reveal powerful principles, but are rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: The twenty-seven prerogative instances (list and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prerogative instances are, ... solitary instances, migrating instances, conspicuous instances, clandestine instances, constitutive instances, similar instances, singular instances, deviating instances, bordering instances, instances of power, accompanying and hostile instances, subjunctive instances, instances of alliance, instances of the cross, instances of divorce, instances of the gate, citing instances, instances of the road, supplementary instances, lancing instances, instances of the rod, instances of the course, doses of nature, wrestling instances, suggesting instances, generally useful instances, and magical instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instances 'excel' ordinary instances by specifically aiding theory or practice. Regarding theory they assist senses (e.g., lamp instances) or understanding: solitary instances expedite exclusive arrival at the form; migrating, conspicuous, accompanying, and subjunctive instances confine and indicate affirmative; clandestine and singular instances elevate to general natures; constitutive and similar instances have lesser immediate force; deviating instances correct habits; bordering instances lead to grand form; cross and divorce instances guard from false forms/causes. Regarding practice they point where to commence (instances of power), measure (four mathematical instances), or elevate practice (generally useful and magical). Treat this taxonomy as a working toolkit for structuring experimental inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which prerogative instances to collect first
rubrics_metrics.description: Out of these twenty-seven instances, some must be collected immediately, without waiting for a particular investigation of properties. Such are the similar, singular, deviating, and bordering instances, those of power, and of the gate, and suggesting, generally useful, and magical instances;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect these immediately because they either assist and cure the understanding and senses, or furnish general practice. The remainder of the prerogative instances should be collected when compiling synoptical tables for a particular nature. A few well-chosen prerogative instances are worth a multitude of ordinary facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and place instances in synoptical tables
rubrics_metrics.description: When, therefore, we are forming our tables they must be searched out with the greatest zeal, and placed in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically search for prerogative and other significant instances and record them in synoptical tables for the work of the interpreter. These tables (concretes, latent processes, latent conformations) form the supports and corrections of induction and are essential preparatory work before deriving general forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject superstition and fable; apply cautious trust to reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The more internal harmony and aversion ... have been either falsely assigned, or mixed with fable, or most rarely discovered from neglect. ... As for fables, they must be totally exterminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept traditional claims of sympathy/antipathy without experimental verification. Where tradition or reports suggest rare harmonies, investigate them 'through tradition, and faithful and honest reports, but without rashness and credulity, with an anxious and, as it were, hesitating degree of reliance.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use analogical correspondences (quantity/density vs conformation) to guide classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and principal distinction between them is this; that some bodies differ considerably in the abundance and rarity of their substance, but correspond in their conformation; others, on the contrary, correspond in the former and differ in the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching for harmonies or grouping phenomena, distinguish whether similarity arises from substance (quantity/density) or from form/conformation. Apply this to minerals, metals, animals, vegetables, and chemical principles (e.g., sulphur-like vs mercury-like correspondences) to generate hypotheses about underlying forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate lunar and celestial harmonies via careful experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor should we omit the harmony between the motion and phenomena of the moon, and their effects on lower bodies, which may be brought together by an accurate and honest selection from the experiments of agriculture, navigation, and medicine, or of other sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlate celestial motions (e.g., lunar phases) with terrestrial phenomena using accurate, selected experiments from relevant applied domains (agriculture, navigation, medicine). Use such cross-disciplinary, experiment-based collections to test claims of celestial influence rather than relying on speculative astrology.
